neighbours.label: a discourse adverb set off inside a clause after its subject (', however,', 'in their turn', ', then,')
fire: The first proposal was cheap and quick. The second proposal, however, offered far more protection to tenants.
The teachers trained the older pupils, and these pupils, in their turn, trained the youngest ones.
Most reviewers loved the film. The audience, however, stayed away in large numbers.
Kant borrowed this idea from Hume, who had, in his turn, borrowed it from Locke.
The model fits the data well. Its predictions, however, are rarely tested outside the lab.
Rome conquered Greece; Greek culture, in its turn, conquered Rome.
The council approved the budget in May. The mayor, however, refused to sign it until July.
Workers were paid more, and they, in turn, spent more at local shops.
quiet: The first proposal was cheap and quick, but the second proposal offered far more protection to tenants.
The teachers trained the older pupils, and these pupils later trained the youngest ones.

notes: Probe: short sentences ~0.05; two-sentence context 0.20-0.33. The - pole is sentence-initial 'And'.
